mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the sponsor entity charter (certificat de constitution / articles of association) and current registry excerpt (extrait de registre)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the sponsor jurisdiction (Registrar of Companies or equivalent judicial authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the origin state, followed by sworn French translation; if origin state is not a party to the Apostille Convention, consular legalization at the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / certificate of existence for the corporate general partner and ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authorities or company registry of the sponsor jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; alternative consular legalization for non-Apostille states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled certified passport copy and proof of residential address for every ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority and local municipal authorities of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or notarized copy certification for EEA-domiciled UBOs)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 1, 10-1 and 22-1 to 22-15 on the Societe en Commandite Speciale); Law of 12 July 2013 on Alternative Investment Fund Managers; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial or private partnership agreement (contrat de societe) constituting the SCSp; if notarial, the authentic act is filed with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for an SCSp; capital commitments are freely determined in the partnership agreement. If the General Partner is registered with the CSSF as an AIFM, it must maintain own funds of at least EUR 125,000 plus, where applicable, 25% of the preceding year's fixed overheads. No escrow account is required for SCSp formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolution of the General Partner of LU_SCSp — Special Limited Partnership, adopted by the General Partner in its general meeting: (1) the final partnership agreement of this Venture Capital General Partner entity is approved as submitted; (2) the subscriptions of all limited partners are accepted, their capital commitments and profit allocations being recorded in Schedule 1; (3) the registered office is established at [Luxembourg address]; (4) the General Partner is appointed as manager and [name] is appointed as authorised officer of the partnership for ordinary administration; (5) the RCS filing, CSSF AIFM registration, banking account opening and entry-into-effect of the governance documents are authorised, each officer acting singly; and (6) this resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and Luxembourg notary engaged by the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalise the partnership agreement, capital commitments, target fund terms and governance arrangements. Verify the identity and eligibility of all partners, including the general partner's corporate authorisations. Issue the draft deed to the notary for compliance review before signature.
required_dossiers: Final draft limited partnership agreement (contrat de societe)
Capital contribution and profit allocation schedule
Identification and address evidence for all partners
CVs and professional references for general partner officers
Business plan and investment policy for the early-stage technology fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel raises legal objections, revise the partnership agreement and resubmit the corrected draft; no notarial filing is made until all comments are resolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement before a Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary selected by the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange physical attendance or valid powers of attorney for all partners. The notary verifies legal capacity and authenticates signatures. The notary then delivers an original notarial deed (expedition) for registration. A private written deed is statutorily permissible for an SCSp, but notarial execution is market standard for institutional venture capital structures.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or national identity cards of the partners
Duly certified resolution of the corporate general partner authorising entry into the partnership
Executed powers of attorney for any remote signatories
Final notarial deed draft prepared by the Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a discrepancy is identified, execute a supplemental rectification act before registration; there is no statutory waiting period for an SCSp.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the RCS / Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS — Registre de Commerce et des Societes, operated by LBR through the eJustice/LBR online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a certified copy of the constitutional deed and the standard RCS registration forms through the eJustice/LBR portal. Indicate the registered office, the general partner, the authorised signatories and the duration of the SCSp. Upon approval, the SCSp receives an RCS number and a Luxembourg national identification number for tax and banking purposes.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed or signed private deed
Completed RCS registration form
Identification documents of the authorised representatives
Proof of registered office address and landlord consent, if applicable
Declarations of non-bankruptcy for the general partner and managers
Power of attorney for any filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the application, provide a corrected form, a clean translation or a notarial confirmation within one month; if rejected, resubmit through the portal with a cover letter resolving the stated deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CSSF statutory licensing or registration for venture capital fund management
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the General Partner qualifies as a full AIFM or as a small AIFM under Article 3(2) of the Law of 12 July 2013. Prepare and file the applicable CSSF application file, comprising governance, own funds, AML/CFT procedures, risk management and programme of operations. The CSSF must grant authorisation or issue a registration confirmation before regulated fund-management activities can be carried out.
required_dossiers: Programme of operations and detailed business plan
Organisational chart and internal governance rules
Own funds calculation and evidence of available own funds
AML/KYC policies and appointment of an AML compliance officer
Risk management, internal control and conflict-of-interest policies
List of responsible managers and statutory auditors
Draft constitutional documents and legal analysis of the managed fund vehicle
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CSSF issues observations, respond in writing within the stated deadline and revise the programme or policies as required; if authorisation is refused, request a reasoned refusal and appeal to the Tribunal Administratif.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance entry into force and ancillary operational registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS/LBR, CSSF, Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), and the Commune of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the final corporate governance documents, open the SCSp bank account, execute officer mandates and obtain the RCS certificate. Register for direct taxation and, if applicable, VAT using the RCS number. Confirm that the office premises have fire safety certification and that workplace health and safety rules are established before deploying staff.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
CSSF authorisation or registration confirmation, if issued
Fire safety certificate for the office premises
Signed governance and officer mandate documents
Tax and VAT registration forms
AML file and intended bank account documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commune objects to the office location, submit the lease contract and building permit; if tax registration is delayed, contact the AEDT with the RCS extract and correct the application through the online rectification procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) — financial sector supervisory authority for the fund-management operating licence
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: CSSF AIFM authorisation under Article 5, or small AIFM registration under Article 3(2), of the Law of 12 July 2013; complemented by RCS/SCSp registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — non-classified office and management activity; no installation listed under the Luxembourg environmental classification regulation; full EIA report not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. No industrial wastewater or VOC point sources. General waste handling must comply with Luxembourg waste-management regulations; any small office emissions are limited to standard municipal heating and ventilation thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps for office premises; structural safety confirmed by the landlord or commune building certificate; occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines prior to staff occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l’enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties and VAT identification; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax, net wealth tax and direct tax file numbers; Administration des douanes et accises (ADA) for customs and EORI registration; Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for commercial registration; single e-government portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://www.myguichet.lu) with public filings on https://www.lbr.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1 — Commercial registration: Incorporate or register the SCSp with the RCS via MyGuichet.lu/eJustice using a notarised partnership agreement (the SCSp is a commercial company under the Law of 23 July 2016; registration is mandatory; no minimum capital requirement). Obtain the RCS number (numéro d’immatriculation) and the Luxembourg Business Register extract. STEP 2 — Tax file: Request a direct tax file number (numéro de dossier) with the ACD for the Luxembourg corporate income tax and municipal business tax assessments; the SCSp is fiscally transparent by default, so the ACD will attribute income to the general and limited partners. STEP 3 — VAT registration: File the VAT declaration of commencement of activity (Form 560) with the AEDT within 15 days of starting taxable operations, either electronically via MyGuichet.lu or in paper form; the AEDT will issue a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU + 11 digits. A foreign entity with no Luxembourg establishment providing services to a Luxembourg taxable person is generally not required to register because the customer applies the reverse-charge mechanism; however, a foreign SCSp/GP that makes taxable supplies in Luxembourg, performs distance sales, or opts for the franchise waiver must appoint a local VAT representative (assujetti établi) if it has no fixed establishment in Luxembourg. STEP 4 — Customs/EORI: Where goods are exported or imported, obtain a Luxembourg EORI number from the ADA (format LU + RCS number) and file customs declarations electronically. STEP 5 — Employer/non-resident partner formalities: Register with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) only if employing staff; non-resident partners are not subject to Luxembourg personal income tax on carried interest unless the profits are attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is by default fiscally transparent: profits, losses, carried interest and management fees are taxed directly in the hands of the partners (no Luxembourg CIT/municipal business tax/net wealth tax at entity level). Available statutory elections: (1) Article 5(1) LIR election — the SCSp may irrevocably elect to be treated as a resident corporate taxpayer (assujettissement à l’impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and thereby become subject to Luxembourg CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; the election is binding on all partners. (2) Hybrid mismatch adjustment elections under Article 168ter LIR (ATAD 2) allowing re-attribution of payments and offsetting of double-deduction/deduction-no-inclusion outcomes. (3) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the VAT Law. (4) Option to waive the small-business VAT franchise exemption (Article 57 VAT Law). (5) At constitutional level, the SCSp may optionally be endowed with legal personality under the Law of 23 July 2016, but this does not automatically alter fiscal transparency absent an Article 5(1) LIR election. There is no US-style check-the-box regime; the Article 5(1) LIR election is the functional equivalence.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 — small-business franchise exemption threshold for annual taxable turnover excluding VAT (Article 57 VAT Law; threshold increased from EUR 30,000 to EUR 35,000 effective 1 January 2023). The exemption is optional (taxable person may waive it). There is no threshold for compulsory registration of a Luxembourg-established entity performing taxable transactions, for intra-community acquisitions (registration required where the acquisitor exceeds EUR 10,000 union-wide distance-selling threshold), or for foreign suppliers that are deemed to have their place of supply in Luxembourg. A venture capital GP/SCSp earning management fees will typically exceed EUR 35,000 and must register from day one.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg applies a phased e-invoicing regime: (1) B2G e-invoicing is mandatory since 1 January 2024 for invoices issued to the Luxembourg public sector, transmitted via the PEPPOL network in the EN 16931 semantic data model and routed through the national e-Factura platform — this includes invoices for fund management services rendered to public pension/reserve funds if such bodies are contracting authorities. (2) B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary (PEPPOL, EDI, or PDF with qualified electronic signature are all accepted); Luxembourg has no real-time fiscal clearance, no API pre-clearance, no digital stamp (bollino), and no continuous transaction controls (CTCs) comparable to Italy or Hungary. (3) The EU ViDA reform, when adopted (expected entry into force mid-2030s), will introduce mandatory EU-wide B2B e-invoicing and digital reporting; Luxembourg has announced readiness to transpose ViDA without early adoption. (4) All e-invoices must be archived in their original electronic format for 10 years in accordance with Articles 84 and 86 of the Luxembourg VAT Law.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations: 0% VAT applies under Article 54 of the Luxembourg VAT Law provided the goods are physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier, the customer, or a third party on behalf of either, and the supplier obtains and retains evidence of export within 90 days of the time of supply pursuant to Article 45a of Implementing Regulation (EU) No 282/2011. Cross-border B2B services to customers established outside the EU: place of supply is outside Luxembourg under Article 10 of the VAT Law (B2B general rule), and the service is therefore outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (effective 0% with no right of artificial input deduction in Luxembourg). Management of special investment funds: management services provided to UCITS, SIF, SICAR, RAIF, or an SCSp fund that qualifies as a 'special investment fund' under the CJEU B-Finance criteria (collective investment of multiple investors, risk-spreading, regulated or equivalent foreign fund) are VAT-exempt without credit under Article 44(1)(c) of the VAT Law — this is the core treatment for a VC GP; if the underlying fund does not qualify, management fees are taxable at 17%. Carried interest and profit allocations to the GP are not consideration for a supply and fall outside the scope of VAT. Capital calls and disposal proceeds of fund investments are outside the scope of VAT. The GP/SCSp must map each revenue stream (management fee, carried interest, transaction break fees, board/consulting fees) separately, because only export-of-goods scenarios trigger the 0% export rate, while qualifying fund management is exempt, and ancillary advisory services may be taxable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — Single Administrative Document (SAD) / electronic export declaration (IE-529) bearing the Movement Reference Number (MRN) issued by Luxembourg Customs (ADA) or the competent EU customs office of export

Transport evidence: Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), CMR or handing-over certificate issued by a carrier/logistics provider confirming physical departure of the goods from EU territory — to be obtained within 90 days from the time of supply
Commercial invoice and sales contract identifying the non-EU buyer, Incoterms, and the exact nature of goods

Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 / payment confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds — functionally required as audit evidence under AML/CRS and Luxembourg trade-finance diligence practice, although EU/Luxembourg law itself imposes no compulsory currency-repatriation certificate
KYC/UBO documentation of the non-EU customer, warehouse dispatch records, and where applicable periodic supplementary declarations and Common Transit Convention documents
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg and EU law impose no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline: the free movement of capital (Article 63 TFEU) guarantees unrestricted transfer of export proceeds, and the 180-day benchmark reflected in this dossier is a trade-finance and documentary-credit convention, not a legal clawback trigger. Audit scrutiny: the AEDT and the ACD may reopen and reassess VAT and income tax within 5 years for good-faith cases and up to 10 years in cases of fraud or absence of good faith; the customs authorities may likewise revoke the 0% export treatment when proof of export is not obtained within 90 days, resulting in retrospective VAT assessment at 17% on the full export value. Clawback of input VAT deductions is automatic where zero-rating or exemption is denied. Penalties: late VAT payment accrues statutory default interest; formal non-compliance fines range from EUR 250 to EUR 12,500; negligent understatement attracts a 10% surcharge on the evaded tax, rising to 50% in cases of intent; criminal tax fraud (Article 2 of the Law of 17 March 1987 and Article 62 of the VAT Law) is punishable by fines up to EUR 25,000 and/or imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years. The GP and the fund are jointly and severally liable for the VAT due on invoices issued by the SCSp; directors and managing partners may face personal liability for fraudulent zero-rating and for failure to correct false export evidence, and reputational damage includes debarment from public procurement and inclusion in the AEDT non-compliant database.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — Luxembourg's Eurosystem central bank, responsible for monetary operations, financial stability and balance-of-payments statistics; Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) — the competent financial-sector and AML/CFT supervisor for credit institutions and payment/e-money institutions; Ministère des Finances — exchange-control policy in the narrow statutory matters (none apply to standard venture-capital treasury flows); European Central Bank (ECB) — ultimate monetary authority of the euro area. No central-bank licence or exchange-control approval is required for an SCSp GP's ordinary treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. The euro is a reserve currency fully convertible for current and capital transactions within the EU's free movement of capital and payments (Article 63 TFEU). Luxembourg imposes no import/export of capital authorisations, no foreign-exchange surrender or rationing, no parallel-market controls and no repatriation ceilings. Capital contributions into the SCSp, reinvestment of proceeds, profit and carried-interest distributions and management-fee remittances may move in any currency with no central-bank approval. Residual friction points are bank-level AML/CFT screening, the BCL's statistical balance-of-payments declaration (filed by the bank, with possible resident-enterprise information requests for direct-investment flows) and investor-side exchange controls in the LP's home jurisdiction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg has no export-proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion ratio or holding-period requirement. Management fees, carried interest and other service receipts denominated in USD or other foreign currencies may be retained in original currency in a Luxembourg foreign-currency account, or converted at arms-length bank rates, without reference to the BCL. The only administrative duty is statistical: cross-border receipts above the de-minimis threshold (typically EUR 12,500 per transaction) are reported to the BCL by the receiving bank as part of the Eurosystem balance-of-payments reporting framework; no export dossier is required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium — viable only as an ancillary rail, not as the primary treasury. Luxembourg-regulated e-money institutions (EMIs authorised by the CSSF/ECB under PSD2) will accept an SCSp where the partnership has an EEA-based general partner and the account mandate is properly executed, but the SCSp's default lack of separate legal personality, the contractual nature of the partnership, and non-EEA UBOs cause many automated KYB engines to reject onboarding. Funds held at an EMI are e-money tokens, not bank deposits, and are outside the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme (Fonds de Garantie Dépôts Luxembourg); balances should be capped at an operational float (recommended below EUR 10,000) and swept daily to a tier-1 bank account. Legal constraints: the EMI account agreement must be signed by the general partner in its own name on behalf of the SCSp, the partnership agreement must empower the GP accordingly, and PSD2/EMD2 permits EMI accounts only for payment services, so an EMI cannot legally hold the long-term escrow or committed capital, which must sit with a licensed credit institution as a deposit.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and UBOs: CSSF practice under Luxembourg's AML Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) and CSSF Regulation 12-02 requires obliged entities to identify natural persons, but it does not mandate a physical interview as a matter of statute. In market practice, however, tier-1 banks require each authorised signatory and each UBO with 10% or more ownership to appear in person at the bank's premises before the account is activated; no fully remote opening is available for a non-EEA-connected SCSp. Remote video KYC is tolerated only for existing bank customers or EEA-resident directors and regulated professionals. For non-EEA GPs, a physical visit with original passports, an apostilled RCS extract and three-month residence proof is mandatory; if a GP is a legal entity, that entity's own UBOs must also appear. Where the SCSp has no legal personality, the GP must sign the account mandate together with notarised evidence of unanimous partner consent. For this Medium_Risk_Enhanced profile, the underwriting committee additionally requires enhanced due-diligence files on all LPs and UBOs, not only standard KYC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and ownership-structure opacity — non-EEA limited partners spread across Cayman, LLC, BVI-feeder and nominee arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial-ownership stack: individual passports, three-month proof of residence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations, corporate registry extracts and constitutional documents for each intermediate feeder; the fund's private placement memorandum and executed limited partnership agreement; a Luxembourg legal opinion explaining the SCSp structure, the GP's management authority, and the absence of nominee or concealment intent; CSSF/RAIF/AIFMD notifications where the fund is regulated; and a bank-sponsored introduction or commercial reference letter from the lead investor's home bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of the RCS registration date; rolling annual deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automated reminder from LBR; failure to cure exposes the SCSp and its managers to criminal prosecution under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 with fines up to EUR 25,000; persistent default may trigger court-ordered strike-off or judicial dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Depot des comptes annuels) - applicable unless all general partners are entities already subject to equivalent publication obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS via MyGuichet e-filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved by the partners within 6 months of financial year-end and deposited within 1 month after approval; by 31 July for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS summons; criminal fine of EUR 500 to EUR 25,000 against responsible managers; refusal of official extracts; risk of court-ordered dissolution or strike-off for repeated non-publication.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Declaration - Beneficial Owners (Declaration des beneficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), administered by LBR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual anniversary filing; initial declaration and each update (partnership-interest transfer, change of general partner, change of control) due within 1 month of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine from EUR 125 up to EUR 1,250,000 under the Law of 13 January 2019; publication of sanctions; non-compliant status can block financing transactions and notarial deeds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CSSF Annual Regulatory Filings - AIFM/ManCo periodic reports and AML/CFT reporting (where the venture-capital GP holds CSSF authorisation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); annual supervisory fee assessed under CSSF tariff schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual report within 6 months of financial year-end; prudential and AML/CFT reports per CSSF circulars and the terms of the authorisation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative measures and fines, public disclosure of sanctions, remedial orders, and suspension or withdrawal of the CSSF licence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of an approved statutory auditor (re viseur d'entreprises agree) when the SCSp exceeds at least two of the three following criteria for two consecutive financial years: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average headcount 25 employees. An audit may also be required by the partnership agreement or by investor-side covenants even below these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified by the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted in place of Luxembourg GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg RBE law (Law of 13 January 2019) does not require a separate annual UBO re-filing; the RBE declaration must be updated within one month of any change, including any transfer of limited-partnership interests or change in beneficial control of the general partner. The operative annual recertification is the RCS annual declaration due within one month of the registration anniversary; an annual internal register audit should reconcile the partner register, transfer ledger and RBE filings, with corrections lodged within one month of the detected discrepancy.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (general and limited partners)
Register of Managers / General Partner decision records
Minute Book of partner resolutions and circular consents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100 - 3,300 per year (EUR 1,000 - 3,000) for a Luxembourg domiciliation agent and corporate administrator
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,500 - 27,000 per year (EUR 6,000 - 25,000) for a non-exempt SCSp certified audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (aggregate Luxembourg City: 17.00% CIT + 1.19% unemployment fund surcharge at 7% of CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent by default and therefore exempt from entity-level CIT; profits are allocated directly to partners. Preferential regimes at partner level: 80% exemption for qualifying IP income (effective ~4.99%); 50% participation exemption for dividends from 10%+ shareholdings; 100% exemption under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; net wealth tax at 0.5% on taxable net assets above EUR 500,000 unless a specific fund exemption applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) - CIT return; e-filing via eTVA portal (accessible through MyGuichet).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 31 December of the year following the tax year when filed electronically; 30 June of the following year for paper filing; non-resident GP entities with no Luxembourg PE must file by 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax year to which the return relates and the closing date of the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Luxembourg calendar year of the permanent establishment; attach domestic fiscal-year certificate if divergent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, RCS number, LEI, tax identification number, registered address, and principal activity (ISIC 6499).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State foreign registered address of the GP if the form is filed by the local fiscal agent for a deemed taxable election.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable profit / commercial result before statutory deductions (management fees, carried interest allocation).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident GPs must attribute Luxembourg-source management fees to a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of qualifying dividend income and 80% IP box exemption; carried interest should not be booked here.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Evidence of 12-month holding and 10% participation to claim Parent-Subsidiary Directive 100% exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 54 - Impôt sur le revenu des collectivités
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of CIT, solidarity surcharge, and municipal business tax on the final taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply DTA profile if the GP is dual-resident; confirm no double counting of foreign PE income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: monthly surcharge of 0.6% of assessed CIT, capped at 10%; administrative fine up to EUR 1,250; refusal to e-file carries an additional EUR 250 penalty; late payment interest accrues at 0.8% per month with forced collection measures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 531 (Déclaration annuelle des sociétés de personnes) - annual transparency allocation statement for the SCSp; filed via eTVA.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline aligned with Form 500: 31 December of the year following the tax year electronically; 30 June paper; non-resident partners must be covered by a local fiscal representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, RCS, LEI, tax office, and confirmation that the SCSp has not elected taxable status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident GPs must attach a Luxembourg tax representative mandate in Section A.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period and audit/confirmation basis (unaudited early-stage GP permitted).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Match the underlying fund's capital-call schedule if differing from calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit/loss allocation to each partner: name, country of tax residence, Luxembourg tax ID, profit-sharing ratio, and allocated amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify beneficial owners behind corporate partners; failure exposes the GP to AML and transparency penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, withholding tax credits, and any carried-interest reclassification statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach TRCs for LPs claiming treaty relief and certify beneficial ownership.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-filing or incomplete allocation results in administrative fines of EUR 500 to EUR 2,000 per affected partner; reassessment at partner level with 0.8% monthly late interest; loss of fiscal-transparency recognition for the SCSp.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 563 (Déclaration de l'impôt commercial communal / ICC) - municipal business tax return; filed together with Form 500 to the Luxembourg direct-tax administration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same deadline as Form 500 (31 December e-filing; 30 June paper); GP entities with a Luxembourg permanent establishment must file independently.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipality where the enterprise or permanent establishment is located and the local tax registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident GP acting through a Luxembourg office must register with the local commune.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit chargeable to communal business tax before the EUR 175,000 basic allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate operating profit according to the Luxembourg activity; avoid double inclusion from the foreign head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Special deduction for equity capital / interest adjustment and capital allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the arm's-length debt-to-equity ratio for the GP financing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final ICC due after applying the municipal multiplier coefficient (Luxembourg City: 6.75%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the correct multiplier of the commune where the permanent establishment is registered.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Same late-filing and late-payment surcharges as Form 500 (0.6% monthly up to 10%; 0.8% late interest); additional enforcement via communal seizure order for arrears.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (10% minimum participation or EUR 1.2 million acquisition value held 12 months); 0% on distributions by a transparent SCSp because such distributions are treated as direct partner allocations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: 1) Submit REN-1 application for exemption at source to the Bureau d'imposition (withholding tax office) of the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration; 2) attach an original or certified copy of the tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by the residence state, apostilled if required; 3) alternatively, reclaim excess withheld tax via REN-2 within the five-year limitation period; 4) provide documentary proof of beneficial ownership and 12-month holding to comply with the CJEU Danish Cases doctrine; 5) maintain TP and substance records to counter Principal Purpose Test challenges.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on intellectual-property royalties paid to non-residents; no treaty limitation. Interest: statutory 15% rate applies only to interest paid to private individual creditors (Art. 148 LIR); interest paid to non-resident corporate lenders is exempt at 0%; most Luxembourg DTAs reduce corporate interest to 0% and royalties to 0% or 5% (subject to MLI Principal Purpose Test).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR - Local File mandatory if consolidated gross turnover reaches EUR 5,000,000 or related-party transactions with a single counterparty exceed EUR 500,000 (financial transactions above EUR 100,000); Master File required when the group consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Report due when group revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply UAE-style ESR codes, but substance is imposed through Art. 6 AAR LIR (GAAR), ATAD interest limitation rules, CJEU jurisprudence, and the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test; administrative practice (Circular L.I.R. 56/1) requires a Luxembourg office, qualified staff, local business direction, and board/meeting minutes. A VC GP SCSp must demonstrate real presence, employment substance, and economic decision-making to preserve treaty benefits and fiscal transparency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of carried interest, management fee income, or capital-gain revenue from the Form 531/500 filings; use of fictitious advisory invoices to shelter GC fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil tax penalty of 50% of the evaded tax plus late interest of 0.8% per month; criminal fine between EUR 250 and EUR 12,500 per count, doubled on recidivism; imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years (Art. 319 LIR).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner are jointly assessed for the evaded corporate tax where willful misconduct is proven; criminal conviction triggers restitution orders, director disqualification, and travel bans for outstanding tax claims above EUR 15,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an SCSp without Luxembourg premises, staff, or local investment decision-making, using the transparent structure solely to channel VC management fees and carried interest into tax-free allocations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterisation under Art. 6 AAR LIR with re-qualified taxable income and a 10% penalty; denial of DTA and EU Directive benefits under the CJEU Danish Cases and MLI Principal Purpose Test; retroactive assessments plus 0.8% monthly interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: GP directors face joint and several restitution of the adjusted tax; in bankruptcy, the action en comblement du passif (Art. 495 of the Law of 10 August 1915) exposes directors to personal liability for the entire tax shortfall.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform KYB/CDD on Limited Partners, concealment of beneficial owners behind multiple SCSp layers, or processing capital-call wires through unregulated shell banks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1.25 million for legal entities under the Law of 12 November 2004; confiscation of proceeds; CRF (Cellsule de renseignement financier) sanctions; imprisonment up to 5 years for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers and directors are personally liable for CDD failures; criminal prosecution applies when intent is shown; travel restrictions and freezing orders may be issued during cross-border AML investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming 0% dividend withholding on payments routed through the SCSp when the ultimate Limited Partner is not the beneficial owner or the 12-month holding condition is not satisfied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive withholding at 15%; penalty of 10% of the under-withheld amount under Art. 174 LIR; 0.8% monthly late-payment interest; denial of refund claims for five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors acting as paying agents are personally liable for uncollected withholding tax if distributions are made before tax settlement; criminal fraud sanctions apply where certificates are falsified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length investment advisory fees to group fund entities; failure to maintain Local File documentation when related-party transactions exceed EUR 500,000 per counterparty or EUR 100,000 for financing flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP adjustment under Art. 56 LIR; upward adjustment of the taxable base to the arm's-length level; penalty of 10% on the additional assessment; 0.8% monthly interest; denial of mutual agreement procedure relief if documentation is absent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorised the pricing are jointly and severally liable for the additional assessments; severe cases trigger professional disqualification and criminal penalties for fraudulent reporting.
